name: Sonic Youth
label: DGC
lede: Sonic Youth spent thirty years retuning guitars, jamming screwdrivers under the strings and getting an art-school crowd onto major-label radio. It ran from a downtown gallery noise festival to the Lollapalooza headline slot, and it ended when the marriage at its center did.

eras.title: From a gallery floor to a name that stuck
eras.text: Thurston Moore and Kim Gordon met in 1980 at the last gig of Moore's band the Coachmen, then tried on Male Bonding and Red Milk before Moore settled on Sonic Youth. Downtown New York in 1981 ran on no wave and art spaces, and Glenn Branca's wall-of-guitars ensemble handed them a guitarist and a first label.

years.cap: Kim Gordon and Thurston Moore, c. 1981
years.h: Noise Fest at White Columns is Sonic Youth's first show
years.p: Kim Gordon, Thurston Moore and keyboardist Anne DeMarinis play the White Columns gallery in New York, borrowing stand-in drummers for three songs.
years.xp:
Gordon later said the sound they were after only arrived once Moore came up with the name Sonic Youth. Before that the band had gone by Male Bonding, Red Milk and the Arcadians.

The festival also delivered their third member: [[Lee Ranaldo|6eb1f3f8-5c5a-41c2-a390-f397a2b824a3]] was on the bill in [[Glenn Branca|7c0735b8-6444-47a3-a244-522fa7925834]]'s electric guitar ensemble. Drummer [[Richard Edson|bf68dbc8-78ee-492d-8be9-36caddd27665]] came in soon after.

years.h: Branca signs them to Neutral; five songs cut inside Radio City
years.p: [[Glenn Branca|7c0735b8-6444-47a3-a244-522fa7925834]] puts Sonic Youth on his Neutral label in December 1981, and the band records the five-song Sonic Youth EP at a studio in Radio City Music Hall. American reviews were uniformly favorable.

years.h: Richard Edson leaves for KONK, and Bob Bert takes the sticks
years.p: [[Richard Edson|bf68dbc8-78ee-492d-8be9-36caddd27665]] quits to play in KONK full-time. [[Bob Bert|205455ca-426d-442d-971f-01cde6dce988]] steps in, and the band's first tour is as support for [[Swans|3285dc48-9505-469d-ad8a-bdf2d3dba632]], who shared their rehearsal room.
years.xp: On a second Swans tour that December, Thurston Moore kept criticizing Bert for not playing in the pocket. By the next record Bert was out and [[Jim Sclavunos|dc24f4fa-1b47-412f-891c-0f0a43664b8b]] was in.

eras.title: Loved in London, shrugged at in New York
eras.text: The drummer seat kept turning over and the New York press shrugged, but Europe paid attention. By 1985 the band had fallen out with Branca's label, made an American horror album with Lydia Lunch, and found the drummer who stayed to the end.

years.h: Confusion Is Sex is louder, and the drummer is number three
years.p: [[Jim Sclavunos|dc24f4fa-1b47-412f-891c-0f0a43664b8b]] drums on the band's first album and quits within months. [[Bob Bert|205455ca-426d-442d-971f-01cde6dce988]] returns on one condition: no firing him after the tour.

years.big: I Killed Christgau with My Big Fucking Dick
years.h: The Village Voice pans a show and Kim Gordon writes back
years.p: After a Voice critic pans a New York show, Gordon sends the paper a scathing letter. Thurston Moore retitles his song Kill Yr Idols in the music editor's honor.
years.xp:
Gordon's letter accused the Voice of not supporting local music. Robert Christgau answered that the paper had no obligation to support anyone.

Moore's reply was the new title above, printed in full. According to Wikipedia, the feud was later settled amicably.

years.cap: Kim Gordon and Thurston Moore, Los Angeles
years.h: Gordon and Moore marry
years.p: Three years into the band, Kim Gordon and Thurston Moore get married. The partnership at the middle of Sonic Youth lasts 27 years.

years.h: Branca falls out with the band and Bad Moon Rising finds two labels
years.p: After a royalty dispute with [[Glenn Branca|7c0735b8-6444-47a3-a244-522fa7925834]], the Martin Bisi-recorded album comes out on Homestead in the US and Blast First in the UK. [[Lydia Lunch|74f2add6-e8b6-4323-a21b-443600379d16]] sings on Death Valley '69, a song inspired by the Manson murders.
years.xp: According to Wikipedia, Bad Moon Rising sold 5,000 copies in the UK and was acclaimed there, while the New York press dismissed it as too arty and pretentious.

years.h: Steve Shelley, ex-Crucifucks, gets the job with no audition
years.p: [[Bob Bert|205455ca-426d-442d-971f-01cde6dce988]] quits, bored after a year of playing Bad Moon Rising front to back. The band had watched [[Steve Shelley|998815d5-03bc-4228-807f-b550c07038d2]] drum for Lansing, Michigan's [[The Crucifucks|efe79e45-5dcd-4099-9438-e4aff57bbeb3]] and hired him on the spot.
years.xp: Bert and Shelley both appear in the Death Valley '69 video, a handover caught on film. Shelley stayed until the end in 2011.

eras.title: SST, Madonna and a candle
eras.text: Signing to Greg Ginn's SST made Sonic Youth the first New York underground band to get national attention. Three albums in three years followed, a joke side project about Madonna, and a double LP that critics still rank at the top of the decade.

years.h: Hendrix to The New York Times, a toxic waste dump to People
years.p: EVOL is the first album on [[Greg Ginn|4f35de64-27ab-4426-95fd-8d454cda4e48]]'s SST and the first national attention for a New York underground band. Robert Palmer of the Times compared it to Jimi Hendrix; People magazine compared it to a toxic waste dump.

years.h: Sonic Youth and Mike Watt become Ciccone Youth
years.p: With ex-[[Minutemen|d4ad0149-d8ae-4105-8009-0221fce9ff35]] bassist [[Mike Watt|568203ae-c27b-4990-8997-09c0d5c0de77]], the band takes [[Madonna|79239441-bfd5-4981-a70c-55c3f15c1287]]'s surname and cuts Into the Groove(y). Watt covers Burning Up on the flip.

years.cap: Sonic Youth, SST press photo for Sister, 1987
years.h: Sister borrows its plot from Philip K. Dick
years.p: A loose concept album drawn from the science fiction writer's life and work. It sells 60,000 copies and becomes the band's first record in the Village Voice's Pazz & Jop Top 20.

years.src: Wikipedia: Sonic Youth · Wikipedia: Daydream Nation
years.h: Daydream Nation arrives as a double LP with a candle on the cover
years.p: Recorded at Greene St. in July and August 1988 for about $30,000, it comes out on Enigma. Teen Age Riot reaches No. 20 on Billboard's Modern Rock chart, the band's first real airplay.
years.xp:
Engineer Nick Sansano's studio charged $1,000 a day. The band stayed up a whole night mixing the three-part Trilogy so it could be mastered the next morning. The cover is Gerhard Richter's 1983 painting Kerze (Candle).

It placed second in the Voice's Pazz & Jop poll and topped the NME, Melody Maker and CMJ year-end lists. In 2005 the Library of Congress added it to the National Recording Registry.

years.h: Enigma pushes Sonic Youth to Geffen's DGC
years.p: Thurston Moore's verdict on Enigma, which Capitol distributed, after distribution problems. The band signs a five-album, $300,000 deal with Geffen that guarantees creative control, then learns it's the smaller DGC imprint.
years.xp: The band was disappointed to land on DGC rather than Geffen proper, but the creative-control clause held for the next eighteen years.

eras.title: Big siblings to the grunge boom
eras.text: On a major label Sonic Youth became the older band the alternative boom looked up to. Gordon talked Nirvana onto DGC, the band opened for Neil Young, and a tour film named the moment. They also lost a friend, and by 1995 they were headlining Lollapalooza.

years.h: Goo puts Chuck D on Kool Thing
years.p: Kim Gordon based the song on her 1989 interview with LL Cool J, and [[Public Enemy|bf2e15d0-4b77-469e-bfb4-f8414415baca]]'s [[Chuck D|88633ac3-c8e2-420f-8415-77ac56b3105f]] guests. Goo sold over 200,000 copies by December.
years.xp:
Gordon, a hip-hop fan, came away from the LL Cool J interview put off by his dismissal of punk and his views on women. Kool Thing reached No. 7 on Billboard's Modern Rock chart. [[Raymond Pettibon|3e603b97-d5f8-4547-891b-74cdfd2ed7bf]]'s cover drawing of two mods in sunglasses is based on a photo of two witnesses in the Moors murders trial.

The record cost $150,000, five times Daydream Nation. Producer Nick Sansano was replaced during mixing by Ron Saint Germain, and according to Wikipedia Sansano was so hurt he wouldn't speak to the band for years.

years.h: Gordon keeps recommending Nirvana until DGC signs them
years.p: That August the two bands play seven West Coast dates together, with [[Dale Crover|9b93a71b-1484-4bea-b096-f660c1161f8a]] drumming for Nirvana.

years.h: Neil Young and Crazy Horse take Sonic Youth into arenas
years.p: On the Ragged Glory tour the band supports [[Neil Young|75167b8b-44e4-407b-9d35-effe87b223cf]] and Crazy Horse, playing noise to Young's crowds.

years.cap: Lee Ranaldo, Shibuya Kokaido, Tokyo, April 1991
years.h: Three weeks across Europe with Nirvana, on camera
years.p: From August 20 to September 1 the band tours Ireland, the UK, Germany, Belgium and the Netherlands with [[Nirvana|5b11f4ce-a62d-471e-81fc-a69a8278c7da]], playing Reading and Pukkelpop. [[Dave Markey|c48f5a63-0b7c-4bbc-b8bb-64474ad7c77c]] films it as 1991: The Year Punk Broke.
years.xp: Sonic Youth is the focus, with time for Nirvana, [[Dinosaur Jr.|77c167d2-4965-4421-830a-9815e4956475]], [[Babes in Toyland|41593aa1-dda6-4a5a-af87-0eebf93e3775]], Gumball and the [[Ramones|d6ed7887-a401-47a8-893c-34b967444d26]]. Several scenes spoof Madonna's tour film Truth or Dare. It opened in theaters in December 1992.

years.h: Joe Cole's murder shapes Dirty
years.p: 100% and JC are about Cole, a friend and former [[Black Flag|9941a936-196a-4a62-ae53-a69cbc33f20e]] roadie killed in a robbery in December 1991. Spike Jonze shoots the 100% video and [[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]] plays on Youth Against Fascism.
years.xp: Cole had been on the 1991 European tour, and 1991: The Year Punk Broke is dedicated to him. Mike Kelley made the Dirty cover art; skater Jason Lee appears in the 100% video.

yt: Bull in the Heather, official video
years.h: No full tour for Experimental Jet Set, still the band's best chart showing yet
years.p: The album hits No. 34 the year Gordon and Moore's daughter Coco is born. With Gordon pregnant there was never a full tour, so many of the songs were never played live.
play: Experimental Jet Set, Trash and No Star

years.h: Fourteen years after a gallery festival, they top Lollapalooza
years.p: Sonic Youth heads the 1995 bill with [[Hole|1dcc8968-f2cd-441c-beda-6270f70f2863]] and [[Pavement|36bfa85f-737b-41db-a8fc-b8825850ffc3]] also on the tour. That year's Washing Machine stretched the band into long improvised pieces.

eras.title: Stolen guitars, a fifth member, a new label
eras.text: The late 1990s were whatever the band felt like: cartoon cameos, a private label for improvised records, a fifth member from Chicago's experimental scene. Then thieves drove off with the instruments, and a band built on custom tunings had to start over.

years.h: Sonic Youth plays itself on The Simpsons
years.p: In the "Homerpalooza" episode the band appears as itself, and its version of the show's theme plays over the end credits.

years.h: SYR: a private label for improvised records
years.p: Each release carries titles and liner notes in a different language. SYR3 (1998) is titled in Esperanto and features [[Jim O'Rourke|172aab84-4c01-4dc0-b2ad-e723033e10ec]].

years.h: Thieves take almost 30 guitars from the van in Orange County
years.p: On July 4 someone empties Sonic Youth's tour van of instruments and stage gear. Some pieces turned up over the next 13 years.
years.xp:
The loss hit harder than it would most bands. Thurston Moore and Lee Ranaldo built songs on custom tunings, often one guitar per song or two, and toured with dozens of instruments. Losing them meant losing the setups.

The band rebuilt with new gear for the Jim O'Rourke-produced NYC Ghosts & Flowers (2000). When some of the stolen instruments came back, they went back to older material on Rather Ripped.

years.h: Chicago's Jim O'Rourke becomes the fifth member
years.p: The producer and multi-instrumentalist, already on SYR3, joins on bass, guitar and keyboards.

years.h: Murray Street is named for the studio's block
years.p: The first album with [[Jim O'Rourke|172aab84-4c01-4dc0-b2ad-e723033e10ec]] as an official member. That year the band also plays the first All Tomorrow's Parties festival.

years.h: Gordon, Moore and daughter Coco play Gilmore Girls
years.p: Kim Gordon and Thurston Moore appear in the season six finale, playing an acoustic What a Waste with Coco.

years.h: Pavement's Mark Ibold takes the bass as O'Rourke leaves
years.p: [[Jim O'Rourke|172aab84-4c01-4dc0-b2ad-e723033e10ec]] goes off to film work and other projects. [[Mark Ibold|003db9eb-2a01-4ece-a5e0-87000aa502d7]], who had played with Gordon in Free Kitten, comes in.

years.cap: Lee Ranaldo and Kim Gordon, Roskilde Festival
years.h: Rather Ripped aims for simpler songs, with Blondie in mind
years.p: Thurston Moore wrote simpler songs, inspired by [[Blondie|4d2956d1-a3f7-44bb-9a41-67563e1a0c94]]'s Parallel Lines. On June 13, 2006, the band plays CBGB for the first time since 1992.
years.xp: The Destroyed Room, a B-sides set that December, was Sonic Youth's final Geffen release.

years.h: After a Starbucks-issued compilation, the band leaves Geffen
years.p: Unhappy with how Geffen promoted its last several albums, Sonic Youth ends the relationship after Hits Are for Squares and signs with Matador Records.

eras.title: Back on an indie, then the end of a marriage
eras.text: On Matador the band made its highest-charting album. Two years later Gordon and Moore separated, and a band that always called itself a democracy couldn't run without its founding couple.

years.h: The Eternal is the highest US peak they ever reach
years.p: Recorded in Hoboken with John Agnello in late 2008, the only Matador studio album reaches No. 18 on the Billboard 200. [[John Fahey|95bb27d2-43c7-4a92-85ee-f95a245f0ee4]] painted the cover.
years.xp: It was Mark Ibold's first studio album with the band. Moore said Ibold locked in immediately and knew the songs better than the rest of them. Sacred Trickster and Antenna were the singles.

years.src: Wikipedia: Kim Gordon · Wikipedia: Thurston Moore
years.h: After 27 years Gordon and Moore announce they're separating
years.p: Gordon later wrote that it followed her finding out about Moore's affair with Eva Prinz, whom he married in 2020.
years.xp:
Gordon confronted Moore about a text message from another woman, according to Wikipedia's account of her memoir. Their divorce was finalized in April 2013.

Moore later moved to London with Prinz. He has said the band was a democracy of sorts and couldn't function while he and Gordon worked things out.

years.cap: Thurston Moore's and Kim Gordon's guitars, Porto
years.h: The last show is in Paulínia, Brazil
years.p: A month after the separation, the band plays the SWU Music & Arts Festival in Paulínia, São Paulo. Lee Ranaldo then says the band is ending for a while.
years.xp: Kim Gordon opens her 2015 memoir Girl in a Band on that last night in Brazil. The score for the French film Simon Werner a Disparu, issued as SYR9 in 2011, was the band's last official release of new music.

eras.title: Nobody announced a breakup
eras.text: Lee Ranaldo asked in 2013 that the band be left to rest in peace, and Moore called it a hiatus. Instead of a reunion came memoirs, a Bandcamp archive of live shows and a 2022 rarities set, In/Out/In.

years.h: Kim Gordon's memoir refers to the split as final
years.p: Girl in a Band covers her art life, the band and the marriage, and refers several times to Sonic Youth having split up for good.

years.h: Thurston Moore answers with Sonic Life
years.p: Doubleday publishes Moore's memoir, his side of the story from Connecticut to downtown New York to the end of the band.
